normalized_text: السَّلامُ عَلَيْكُم Assalamu 'Alaykum brothers and sisters.. (Peace be upon you) So, I've been meaning to make this video for a while now, It's about a specific group of people who like to name themselves "Quranists" or "Quran Alone" or whatever it is, When they are in reality just what we call "Hadith Rejectors" They are a group of people who are spreading today, they are spreading amongst the ignorant Muslims, People who have not studied their religion, they've not studied Hadith, they've not studied the Quran, Who are not aware of Usool أصول (the Fundamental Principles) that a person should have as a Muslim, And they're also spreading among the Reverts –people who are new Muslims– and the reason they are spreading among reverts because some of these reverts obviously, they come from a Christian background and have a skepticism towards the Bible So they tend to compare the Bible with the Hadith and then they come to this kind of fear that: "You know what! Just like the Bible has been corrupted, perhaps the Hadith has been corrupted as well" And then they seep into using their doubts and manipulate those individuals because Obviously they're not aware even of what Hadith is and what is the history of Hadith or any of that So they seep into this type of group of people And obviously, it's mainly one of two reasons why a person would become a Hadith rejecter and rejects Hadith Either it's complete ignorance, meaning that he came across something; came across Ahadith, came across a doubt, And he could not find an answer for it due to his ignorance; he completely decided to reject Hadith as a wholesale, Or reject a group of Ahadith he doesn't like because he couldn't find an understanding for these Ahadith. So that's one reason And the other reason is desires. People who want to interpret the Quran the way they want, Who don't want to follow a specific kind of teachings in the Hadith They want to do things their own way and because of their own desires and wanting to avoid all of these different types of things, They end up in the end rejecting Hadith and pretending that they are following the Quran And you know the interesting thing about this group of people is the fact that The same Hadith that they deny has prophesied their coming, and the Prophetﷺ mentioned that this group of people will come So us, as Muslims who follow the Quran, who follow the Hadith, who as any Muslim should be.. We're not really surprised by their existence, they're not really a new group of people coming; But there is a need for clarification for the individuals and the people who don't understand who these people are So the Prophetﷺ in that Hadith which they themselves reject, he said: يوشِكُ أنْ يقعُدَ الرجلُ مُتَّكِئًا على أَرِيكَتِهِ [There will come a time when you'll find that a man reclining on his couch..] Why did the Prophetﷺ say reclining on his couch? There are many reasons why the Prophetﷺ said that The Prophetﷺ is alluding to his arrogance for example, the way he's reclining on his couch like the kings used to recline on their couches So he's implying that this person has arrogance in his heart He's also implying the reality that this individual has not done much work; he's just reclining, relaxing.. He thinks he knows what he's doing, he thinks he understands what he's talking about And then him reclining on his couch what is he going to say: يُحَدَّثُ بحديثٍ مِنْ حديثي [So someone will narrate to him a Hadith from my Hadith] So someone will narrate something about me, which is basically what Hadith is; so someone will mention a Hadith of the Prophetﷺ [Then he says] فيقولُ Then this man who's sitting on the couch, what is he going to say? بينَنَا وبينَكُمْ كتابُ اللهِ [Between us and you is the book of Allah] فما وجدْنا فيه مِنْ حلالٍ اسْتَحْلَلْناهُ [What we find in it Halal, we take it as Halal, and what we find in it Haram, we say it's Haram then] And then the Prophetﷺ responded to them: ألَا وإِنَّ ما حرَّمَ رسولُ اللهِ مثلَ ما حرَّمَ اللهُ [That which the Messenger of Allahﷺ says is Haram, it is the exact same as if Allah is telling you it is Haram] It is the same thing.. Why?! Because as Allahﷻ says in the Quran (Annajm53:3-4) وَمَا يَنطِقُ عَنِ الْهَوَىٰ*إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْيٌ يُوحَى [He does not speak of his own, rather it's Revelation from Allah coming down to the Prophetﷺ] So those individuals.. They've been already spoken about by the same Hadith Which is what people would refer to as irony even though that term is not necessarily correct.. But this is the reality; they are rejecting the Hadith and the Hadith is exactly describing them! Describing the fact that they are people of arrogance, who have not done research, Who don't understand what Hadith is or the sciences behind it, and they're reclining on their couch And then they say: "What we find in the Quran is Halal, and what we don't find there is Haram" Also 'Umar ibn alKhattab, he alluded to these individuals by saying that there was the verse of رجم (Rajm: stoning) The verse that talks about stoning the adulterers - persons who commits adultery- in the Quran and this verse was uplifted It was abrogated, as the Quran mentions in many places that there is abrogation So that verse was abrogated, and then 'Umar ibn Alkhattab said that (the Prophetﷺ, he stoned a person who committed adultery); After the verse was abrogated and then he said (Abu Bakr did as well), and then he said (and we did as well) And then he says (and I'm afraid that if time goes by, a group of people will come and they're going to say) Exactly what those Hadith rejecters say today, they will say: (that we don't find stoning in the Quran), you know! فيضلُّوا بتركِ فريضةٍ أنْزلَها الله تعالى (So they become misguided by leaving an obligation that Allahﷻ has revealed) So 'Umar ibn Alkhattab here is saying what? He's exactly talking about these group of people You'll find these group of people completely denying stoning and say that stoning is not in the Quran, this punishment is barbaric.. And obviously they're influenced by liberalism and this and that, and their desires and many reasons that we already mentioned But you see how the Hadith -the same Hadith that they reject- completely speaks about the reality And speaks about what they will do in the future, which we can see and observe with our own eyes So this is a sign for us, for people who accept the Hadith and people who understand the historicity of the Hadith That these people are not new people that are coming, but these people have been foretold by the Prophetﷺ And even spoken about by his Companions; the likes of 'Umar ibn Alkhattab who was second Caliphate of Islam This video here is going to be kind of divided into three parts.. In the first part; positive arguments for why Hadith is a necessity for every Muslim And I'll make different types of arguments, I'll give reasons And in all of these parts, I'll try to depend on two things I'll depend on the Quran itself because they pretend that they accept the Quran And I'll also depend on common sense, you know.. Common Sense which I'm hoping the people watching this video will at least have if they're sincere And I'd recommend people to actually watch the entire video, not to take a part and then go run with it and try to refute a small part No, watch the whole thing and then come to your conclusion if you are sincere If you're not sincere then this is not for you anyways because you're not looking for the Truth So first I'm going to make these positive arguments as the first part The second part I'm going to give logical criticisms and reasoning also from the Quran, why those people are inconsistent And they're completely illogical in their methodology and approach when we actually scrutinise it and look at it And in the last part I'm going to speak about the historicity of Hadith, why do we accept Hadith? And the historicity of Hadith? and all of that, which is going to be very beneficial InshaAllah (If God wills it) So this video is not just for these group of people, it's not just for the ignorant people who got misguided by them It's also for every Muslim so they can benefit by one of two ways, either learning how to refute those individuals InshaAllah If they come across them and if they present doubts to you, and obviously you yourself learning the importance of Hadith And its origins in the Quran and its origins in the Islamic Revelation and also learning what Hadith is and its historicity and all of that So it's going to be very beneficial InshaAllah, so bear with me InshaAllah And the time, this video could be a little bit long but not too long InshaAllah, Because I'll even try to summarise it and not speak about too many things So bear with me InshaAllah because, for this time, do احتساب (Ihtisab: that this time is for the sake of Allahﷻ) And for your benefit as a Muslim. I know a lot of people have a TikTok kind of time attention or time span or whatever it is, But InshaAllah try to listen to this video and you'll find it very beneficial for everyone.. I will move into the first part InshaAllah The first argument I want to present is a simple idea, this idea is: that the Quran mentions certain information This certain information has been mentioned by the Prophetﷺ in the Quran, So Allah quotes the Prophetﷺ saying certain things in the Quran So first I want to establish a general rule and a principle that as Hadith rejecters, they have to accept because it's in the Quran Allahﷻ says about the Prophetﷺ (Alhaqqa69:44-46) وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ الْأَقَاوِيلِ* لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ * ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنَا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ [If the Prophetﷺ were to make up certain statements and lies about Allahﷻ, Allahﷻ is going to seize him..] Meaning that he is going to die.. Allahﷻ is going to cause him to die and is going to punish him So that means that the Prophetﷺ has no possibility of making up information about Allahﷻ I'm sure us and the Hadith rejecters agree on that, but they completely deny any information from him anyways But we agree on the principle that the Prophetﷺ cannot make up statements about Allah, because if he did he would be dead Based on that verse of Quran that you accept, and we already mentioned that the Prophetﷺ what he speaks is Revelation anyway So Allahﷻ says in the Quran a statement about the Prophetﷺ in chapter:3 (Al'imran) of the Quran verse:124, Allahﷻ says: إِذْ تَقُولُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَلَن يَكْفِيَكُمْ أَن يُمِدَّكُمْ رَبُّكُم بِثَلَاثَةِ آلَافٍ مِّنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُنزَلِينَ Allah is saying: [When you said to the believers O'Prophet, isn't it sufficient for you that Allah is going to give you 3000 angels descending?] Now my question is to those Hadith rejecters who only pretend the only Revelation that was revealed is the Quran And there's no other sources of Revelation and all the Hadith are not reliable and we don't accept information from the Hadith Or we don't accept history and all of that, it's only the Quran -the Quran alone- is the only thing you accept.. Now the question is: Where did Allahﷻ say to the Prophetﷺ that Allah is going to enforce him with 3000 angels? Find me a verse in the Quran where Allahﷻ before told the Prophetﷺ that he's going to enforce him with 3000 angels Then the Prophetﷺ went and told this information to the believers, because if that information is not in the Quran And the Quran is the only Revelation, then where did the Prophetﷺ get this information? That there is 3000 angels that Allah is going to enforce the believers with? You've got no option except to accept that there is another Revelation revealed to Prophetﷺ Where he was told that he will be enforced by 3000 angels, unless -as I said- you pretend That the only source of Revelation is the Quran, find us that verse Where is that verse in the Quran where Allah told the Prophet that he's going to enforce him with 3000 angels?! So that's example number:1, example number:2.. And there's many many examples by the way, I'll just give few examples on this argument Second example is Allahﷻ for example says in the Quran chapter:2 (Albaqara), verse:142: سَيَقُولُ السُّفَهَاءُ مِنَ النَّاسِ مَا وَلَّاهُمْ عَن قِبْلَتِهِمُ [The ignorant of the people, they will say why did they move away from their Qibla (direction of prayer)] Then Allahﷻ says moving forward in the verse:143, Allah says: وَمَا جَعَلْنَا الْقِبْلَةَ الَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيْهَا إِلَّا لِنَعْلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ الرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ So Allahﷻ says: [we made] وَمَا جَعَلْنَا.. And جَعَلْنَا here is referring to Allah. Allah is The One Who "made" according to the Quran [Allah made the previous Qibla as a test to see who will follow the Messenger and who will turn on his back] So now the question is: In this verse, Allah says direct yourself to Mecca, But Allah also says in the same verse that he made the previous Qibla a direction, He's The One Who made it.. Now find me in the Quran where is this command to follow the first Qibla, the Qibla before Mecca.. Where is that command in the Quran? Because Allahﷻ is saying we made the previous Qibla, Which means that the command to pray to a different Qibla before Mecca was from Allah. Now the question is: Where is it in the Quran did Allah command the Prophet or the believers to pray to a different Qibla other than Mecca? Because this verse here speaks about a different Qibla that Allah commanded the believers to follow If you cannot find it, then if you're a sincere person and you have any intellect, then you'd have to admit that there is another source Of Revelation other than the Quran where this information was, by Revelation, conveyed to the Prophetﷺ Not through the Quran, but through another source of Revelation The 3rd example I'm going to give for this specific argument InshaAllah and we end with this example, Is Allahﷻ says in the Quran chapter:2 (Albaqara), verse:187: أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَائِكُمْ [Allahﷻ has now made it permissible for you to have intercourse with your women in the night of fasting] In the nights of Ramadan, the nights of fasting, you can have intercourse with your women.. And Allah says that: He knows that you used to betray yourselves عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ كُنتُمْ تَخْتَانُونَ أَنفُسَكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَعَفَا عَنكُمْ [So he forgives you for basically disobeying his command and betraying yourselves in the past, so now..] فَالْآنَ بَاشِرُوهُنَّ [So now you're allowed to be intimate with them] Where is that command where Allahﷻ told them that they cannot have intercourse with them in the night? Because Allah is saying now you can, it has become Halal حلال (permissible) for you now, It's become permissible for you to have intercourse in the night of fasting So where is the first command where Allah said that you cannot do it? Same question again, where is that command in the Quran? If you cannot find that command in the Quran, then you have to accept the reality, The fact, that there is another source of Revelation other than the Quran So that is the first argument that we have which is a positive argument for the Hadith Which shows that there is another Revelation other than the Quran. So that's the first argument.. The second argument that we're going to talk about is that the Quran speaks about something that it calls "wisdom" حكمة (Hikma) If you want to translate it into wisdom or you want to translate into something else, But Hikma in the Arabic language is referred to as wisdom, this is the most common meaning of the word Hikma So Allahﷻ speaks about something that is called Hikma in the Quran And here before I give this argument, I want to talk about something very absurd And something very important to keep in mind, because we will speak about it in the future as well.. In the Arabic language and even in the English language and other languages, You have a word that is used for conjunction between two words. Like for example: "I like bananas and oranges".. So when you say "and" you use it to have a conjunction between two things that are different from each other You don't say: "I ate pineapple and pineapple". So when you use the word "and" for conjunction, It is not between the same thing, it is between two things that are different from one another This is in English and it's the same in Arabic; when you say وَ (Wa) Like I met.. قابلتُ زيداً وعمرو (I met Zayd and 'Amr) You do not say in Arabic: "I met Zaid and Zaid" قابلتُ زيداً وزيداً So the وَاو (waw), the letter و (wa) which is translated into "and" in English, is used for conjunction It is used for two things that are different from one another, because what those Hadith rejecters tend to do is that they throw around all logic, and they try to pretend that the word "and" is speaking about the same thing And I will give examples for why they have to do that, they have no choice except doing that, and we'll speak about that now So we said the second argument here is talking about something called Alhikma (Wisdom) So Allahﷻ says in the Quran in multiple different places, that He's revealed something called Alhikma So that Hikma is Revelation from Allahﷻ and that Hikma is not the Quran, it's something other than the Quran Why is it something other than the Quran?! You look at the Quran chapter:2 of the Quran verse:231: وَمَا أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنَ الْكِتَابِ وَالْحِكْمَةِ [And what He revealed to you from the Kitab "the book" (i.e. the Quran), and the Hikma] So here we have two things: We have the Kitab, which is the Quran, and the Hikma and both of them are Revelation Allah is saying وَمَا أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكُم [What He revealed to you] In another place as well in chapter:4 (Annisa') of the Quran verse:113, Allah speaks directly to the Prophet; he says: وَأَنزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ [Allah revealed to you, O'Prophet Alkitab (i.e Quran), and the Hikma] Alkitab here is the Quran, because that is what was revealed to the Prophetﷺ or upon the Prophetﷺ, and the Hikma So we have something called Hikma that's revealed from Allah and we'd like those Hadith rejecters to tell us what is this Hikma? Why do they have to tell us what is this Hikma? Because that Hikma is not only Revelation from Allah, but it's also something that is being taught to the believers And who is teaching it? It is the Prophetﷺ.. And it cannot be the Quran because we already said that Allah mentioned that it is something else other than the Quran, Allahﷻ says in the Quran commanding the Prophetﷺ or mentioning to us -as believers- in chapter:2 (Albaqara), verse:129:) وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ [that Messenger will teach us the Book (the Quran) and the Hikma] So that Hikma which is revelation from Allah is going to be taught by the Messenger, and it is not the Quran So my question is now for those Hadith rejectors.. Where is that Hikma that is being taught by the Prophetﷺ? Where can we find it? In which book is it? Because it's other than the Quran I وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتَابَ He already [teaches them the Quran], so you cannot say it is the Quran.. وَالْحِكْمَةَ So I would like you to share with us and show us where is that Hikma that the Prophetﷺ was teaching..? And that is mentioned in many verses of the Quran like (Albaqara2:151) [teaches them the Quran (Kitab) and the Hikma] And many many verses of the Quran; chapter:3 (Al'imran) verse:164, again saying that: [He teaches them his verses and he teaches them the Kitab (Quran) and he teaches them the Hikma] So the Hikma is other than the Kitab, that is something that is being taught by the Prophetﷺ. It is Revelation from Allah Not only that, it is something that is recited or said out loud because Allahﷻ says in the Quran chapter:33 (Alahzab), verse:34: وَاذْكُرْنَ مَا يُتْلَىٰ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَالْحِكْمَةِ [And mention and recite what you hear in your houses from the verses of Allah which is the Quran and the Hikma] So what is this Hikma? what is this Revelation taught by the Prophetﷺ and being recited out loud and it is not the Quran?! Now we would like those Hadith rejecters to explain to us and tell us– Because as أهل السنة (Ahl Assunnah: People of the Sunnah) we say that the Hikma is clearly -without a shadow of a doubt- It is the Hadith, the explanations of the Prophetﷺ which expounds on the Quran, And you see that mentioned very clearly in chapter:16 (Annahl) of the Quran, verse:44, where Allahﷻ says: وَأَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الذِّكْرَ [So we revealed to you the Dhikr], Dhikr here we say it is the Sunnah.. لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ مَا نُزِّلَ إِلَيْهِمْ [So you can explain to the people that which was revealed to them before] So there is something that was revealed to the people that the Prophetﷺ is going to explain using another Revelation So there's two Revelations there: وَأَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الذِّكْرَ / مَا نُزِّلَ إِلَيْهِمْ There's two things here are mentioned; Dhikr is mentioned and something else that was revealed We say that something else that was revealed is the Quran And Dhikr here is the Hikma -the Sunnah- that the Prophetﷺ is going to use to explain to the people But regardless whether you -as a Hadith rejector- want to give the interpretation of the Dhikr or not, You want to accept this as the Sunnah or not, or you want to say that the Hikma is the Sunnah or not, You still have a problem to deal with. And that problem is that all of these verses are mentioning something other than the Quran And it is saying that the Prophetﷺ is teaching it and it is for us as believers So the question is for you and me as a believer now, where do we find the other thing that the prophet is teaching? So it's a Prophetic teaching -not the Quran- we already established it's something other than the Quran Can you tell us now, as a Hadith rejector, where do we find the other source of information that is not the Quran? That is being taught by the Prophetﷺ? We'd like to hear your input. You can tell us what the Hikma is If you don't want to tell us what the Hikma is, you can explain to us what is that thing That the Prophetﷺ is going to teach, that is other than the Quran? So that is the second argument The third argument is quite basic. That argument is a basic, clear cut command in the Quran and it will come back to a point That we mentioned as well, and that point is the word "and", which is a conjunction between two different things There are tens, literally tens of verses in the Quran, and you can even say hundreds if you want to combine Just the meaning of obedience towards Allah and the Messenger in the Quran; you'll find tens of verses Now I'm going to mention just some of these verses that are in the Quran, And then I'm going to ask a question to those Hadith rejectors that they can perhaps explain to us. Allahﷻ says in the Quran: (Alimran3:132) وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ [Obey Allah and the Messenger that you may attain peace] Allahﷻ says (Annisa4:59) يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ [O' who you believe obey Allah and obey the Messenger] Allahﷻ says (Almaida5:92) وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ [And obey Allah and obey the Messenger] Allahﷻ says (Alanfal8:20) أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ [Obey Allah and His Messenger] Allahﷻ says (Alanfal8:46) وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلَا تَنَازَعُوا فَتَفْشَلُوا [Obey Allah and His Messenger] Allahﷻ says (Annoor24:54) قُلْ أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ [Say obey Allah and obey the Messenger] Allahﷻ says (Annoor24:56) وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ [Just obey the Messenger].. The Messenger alone here, without even obeying Allah Allahﷻ says (Muhammad47:33) يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ [O' you who believe obey Allah and obey the Messenger] Allahﷻ says (Attaghabun64:12) وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ [Obey Allah and obey the Messenger] And these are all different verses.. I'm not just repeating the same verse These are all different verses that are all essentially saying obey Allah and obey the Messenger, Or obey Allah and His Messenger, and there are many verses; I'm not going to mention all of them And they're mentioned in different wordings, like for example: [Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him into paradise] (Annisa4:13) [And who obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah] (Annisa4:80) [And who obeys Allah and the Messenger.. he will be from those that Allah has bestowed favor upon] (Annisa4:69) So they're all saying the same thing essentially, but all of it in different wordings and tens of verses in the Quran When you speak to a Hadith rejectors, they try to pretend the word "and" doesn't mean "and", and it is not a conjunction between 2 things So it's not like the obedience of Allah is different from the obedience of the Messenger We would say that makes zero sense for many reasons: First, we would say that would render the meaning of the words of Allah meaningless Because essentially Allah is saying -the Hadith rejectors say- when Allah says obey the Messenger, It is referring to the Quran or it's referring to obeying Allah. So then we would say that renders the Quran meaningless! Why? Because it would mean that all of these verses are saying obey Allah and obey Allah, obey Allah and obey Allah,.. So that is the meaning of the verses according to those Hadith rejectors, and these are tens of verses! The Authentic Hadith is that which is transmitted from the Prophetﷺ by a person who is trustworthy A person who is known in his community to be a trustworthy individual, Who is a good individual and he's a practicing Muslim, and he’s a strong memoriser عدل ضابط The 1st condition is that he is a trustworthy individual, 2nd is that his memorisation and memory is very strong If it becomes weaker then he's no longer fitting that criteria So whoever he narrates from, has to also have these 2 conditions: Has to be strong in memory and has to be a good individual known in the community to be a good individual And the Chain has to be Connected. The Chain has to go all the way back to the Prophetﷺ, there cannot be any people missing in the Chain You cannot narrate from someone that was not living at your time, that was living 200 years before you Because you cannot meet him or you cannot take information from him. So it has to be possible for you to meet that individual Not only that, but also the Chain has to go all the way back to the Prophet If the information reaches a Companion of the Prophet only, but it does not reach the Prophetﷺ, and he doesn't say the Prophet said, Then that is a statement of a Companion, it is not a Hadith of the Prophetﷺ If it reaches a student of a Companion, then it is not a Narration of the Prophetﷺ, Rather it is a statement of a follower, of a Companion of the Prophetﷺ This is what Authentic Hadith is. That which is narrated by a trustworthy, just individual, well memoriser; a strong memory, Who narrates from someone like him, tracing all the way back to the Prophetﷺ And it cannot be irregular, they cannot have any defects, that Narration cannot have any defects Now defects and irregularity, these are like.. big things; that there's a whole Science written on that But I'll give a very basic example of شذوذ (Shudhudh: irregularity), which is for example where you have one person who told the story, And then there was six people sitting down, five of those people narrated the story in a way, And one individual narrated the same story, but he added extra information that the other five did not say, That would mean that this extra part that was added is either a mistake or irregularity It is something.. the Narrator has made a mistake in attributing it to that Narrator when he did not narrate it So we know that; through tracing all of those different Chains of Narrations and we look at those people who narrated the Hadith, And we see if the majority are narrating one thing, and just one person who had an extra statement that the other people did not narrate –even though they've all heard the story from the same person– Then, we say the extra statement that was made is irregular and that statement can be rejected Also the idea of hidden defects; there are defects that can remove the reliability of a Hadith And there are defects that don't remove the reliability of the Hadith, the Hadith can be Authentic even though there's a hidden defect For instance, if we say that the Narrator says I heard from Ibn 'Umar, which is a Companion of the Prophet, And he actually heard it from Abu Hurayra, so both of those two different people are reliable, But the Narrator there's a hidden defect there, he made a mistake and he heard it from a wrong person He did not hear it from 'Abdullah Ibn 'Umar, he actually heard it from Abu Hurayra But he mixed the two individuals. So that's a defect, but a hidden defect Another hidden defect for example is someone narrates information; he attributes it to the Prophet, While actually, it was not from the Prophetﷺ but it was a story that was heard from the people of the Scriptures That, would be considered a hidden defect, and it will affect the Hadith Now the Hadith is no longer an Authentic Narration that you have to believe in Rather it's information taken from the people of the Scriptures As I said, I don't want to go into very strict details to show you how much those people who are rejecting Hadith Have no clue of how much work the people have put to authenticate these Narrations, And for us to come to this conclusion: these Narrations have to be historically reliable, So it's not just like we found the letter and the king was signing it, but we know who the king is, We have the full biography of the king, we know who wrote the letter, which handler of the king wrote the letter, We know his student who took the letter from him, and we know his son and his son and his son and his friend And whoever narrated that information until it reaches today, seeing it in front of our own eyes This is our criteria, not the criteria of the weak Western history that you accept, but our criteria is even further and much stricter for us to accept anything coming from the Prophetﷺ or not coming from the Prophetﷺ And how precise were those people actually in passing down the information I'll give two very basic examples: There's a great scholar who's called Yahya Ibn Ma'een Yahya Ibn Ma'een is a great scholar who used to handle the grading of Ahadith and seeing who is reliable and who's not One day –they have something called TESTING the person who narrates the Hadith– As we said, the person who narrates Hadith has to have a strong memory, So what they do is that they used to TEST the reliability of the memory of these individuals, –the people that are known to be trustworthy that narrate Narrations of the Prophetﷺ–, they used to go and test them Yahya Ibn Ma'een went one time to one of his teachers, Alfadl Ibn Dukayn, who is a major scholar, well known of strong memory But even though he was well known of strong memory, and in the community they know that this person has a strong memory, They said still, we have to actually investigate, we have to actually see whether he has a strong memory or not, let’s actually test him So what Yahya Ibn Ma'een did, is that he went to him and then he mixed some of his Narrations with another person's Narrations In order for him to test Alfadl Ibn Dukayn whether, he actually has a strong memory or not So that was a regular thing the scholars used to do at the time, they used to go to different Narrators and they used to test them And you do not know when they're going to test you, who is going to test you So, if you have a weak memory, then they will label you after testing you that you have a weak memory, And then people -whoever narrates from you- that Narration would be not reliable, Will be doubted because the memory of that individual is not strong Also for example Yahya Ibn Ma'een –they were very specific–, he used to sit in a sitting, and a person narrates Hadith, And then there are students who are taking the Hadith and writing it down.. So, Yahya Ibn Ma'een noticed one individual who slept. So then YIM wrote down at which number of the Hadith did he sleep He slept when the 4th Hadith was being narrated, And then when he woke up again, Yahya Ibn Ma'een wrote down that he woke up at the 11th Hadith So they were so strict to make sure what he directly heard and what he did not hear If that individual leaves the sitting of knowledge and goes and narrates a Hadith, they will say to him: "Where did you hear this Hadith from? You were sleeping" "We know that you didn't hear this Hadith from that sitting, so where did you get this information from?" They were so strict to the extent of making sure that the individuals, even though they're sitting down In the same sitting of knowledge, that they're writing down what exactly they heard 100% And we can even see this idea of reliability, it was from the beginning From the time of the first Caliphate of Islam, right directly after the death of the Prophetﷺ The first Caliphate of Islam who ruled only for like 3 years after the Prophetﷺ, In his time they were still questioning people when they bring information For example, there was a grandmother or an old woman who came to Abu Bakr AsSiddiq and she said: "Do I have anything from inheritance?". Then another Companion, Muhammad Ibn Maslama, he also said "I heard this information". يوشِكُ أنْ يقعُدَ الرجلُ مُتَّكِئًا على أَرِيكَتِهِ [There will come a time when you'll find that a man reclining on his couch..]

ألَا وإِنَّ ما حرَّمَ رسولُ اللهِ مثلَ ما حرَّمَ اللهُ

وَمَا يَنطِقُ عَنِ الْهَوَىٰ*إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْيٌ يُوحَى

Describing the fact that they are people of arrogance, who have not done research,
